title: fr:in-progress is never removed when a batch finishes: 197 closed issues still say an agent is working on them
body:
## What happened

`fr triage batch dispatch` sets `fr:in-progress` on every member issue (spec 2026-09-25 triage-batches d7, §3 item 1). Nothing removes it when the batch finishes. `batch cancel` is the only path that takes the label off. The batch PR's merge closes the issue through `Closes #n`, and the label stays.

Measured 2026-10-07 on derio-net/super-fr:

- **197 closed issues** still carry `fr:in-progress`, closed between 2026-09-26, the first batch, and today. The newest is #1051, closed by batch `checks-latest-run` (#1052). The driver released its `fr:claimed` correctly in the same pass (`release super-fr#1051 (checks-latest-run): released`); `fr:in-progress` was left behind.
- Three open issues carry it, all legitimately: #1073 (batch dispatched), and #1074 and #333 (claimed by another scope).

The label's own definition says "An agent is actively working on this" (`fr/labels.py`, `FR_IN_PROGRESS`). On a closed issue that is false.

## Why it matters

- The triage engine itself is not misled: `stage.py` ranks `closed` above `in-progress`, so a closed issue derives as closed.
- The forge is misled, and the forge is the shared surface that #1043's claims model treats as the coordination channel between scopes and hosts. A label filter such as `label:fr:in-progress` returns 200 issues for 3 real ones. That makes the label useless as a signal for a human, another scope or any other tool.
- `collect` reads comments for every `fr:in-progress` issue (claims spec §3, "Collect reads comments only for `fr:in-progress` issues"). That is bounded only as long as the label stays on open issues; a reader that widens to closed issues would read these too.

## Proposal

1. **Remove on finish.** Remove `fr:in-progress` from a batch's members at the same moment the driver releases their claims, when the batch is finished (archive PR merged). Use the same rule as release: only from members this scope dispatched, never from a member another scope holds (claims R6). `batch merge` outside the driver should do the same for the members it closes.
2. **One-off cleanup** of the 197 already stale. The operator can run this once 1 ships, or right now:
   ```
   gh issue list -R derio-net/super-fr --state closed --label fr:in-progress --limit 500 --json number --jq '.[].number' \
     | xargs -I{} gh issue edit {} -R derio-net/super-fr --remove-label fr:in-progress
   ```
   Alternatively, a `fr triage check` set "closed but labelled in-progress" could print that command for any scope.

## Acceptance

- Once a driven batch's archive PR merges, none of its closed members carries `fr:in-progress`. A member held by another scope keeps it.
- `check`, or the board, names closed issues still labelled `fr:in-progress`, so drift from manual closes is visible.

title: Driver: recover a batch PR that goes red after the train updates it (re-update on main moving, else hand back to the session)
body:
## What happened

On 2026-10-07 the wave driver's merge train updated batch PR #1052 (`checks-latest-run`) from main at 02:37 (`chore: update from main`, f853f1e). The PR had been green at 02:32. Main was briefly broken at that moment: #1058 had landed a run cursor at version 8 just after the run kind moved to 9. The release's `fr migrate artifacts --yes` fixed main shortly afterwards.

The update pulled main's broken state into the branch, and 11 checks went red (stale-cursor failures in `validate-artifacts` and the test shards). From then on, every pass printed

    train derio-net/super-fr: no head · stepped over checks-latest-run (#1052)

for about three hours. The driver also warned three times, `warn checks-latest-run: PR #1052 CI failing at f853f1effc59`. Meanwhile:

- the driver never updated the branch again, because it updates only a PR whose CI is passing. By then the branch was 14 commits behind a main that would have fixed it;
- the batch session was idle and was never told;
- the last wave could not finish. A manual hand-off to the session started recovery.

## The gap

The driver hands work back to a session for merge conflicts (#959) but has no recovery path for a red PR. A red batch PR has two causes, and the driver can tell them apart:

1. **Red from the driver's own update.** The PR was green at its previous head, and the red head is a driver-made `chore: update from main` merge. The batch's diff did not change; main did.
2. **Red from the batch's own work.** The failing head is a session commit.

## Proposed recovery

- **Case 1:** when main moves past the base the driver merged, update the branch again, despite red CI, at most once per new main sha. This is often enough: main's own repair arrives by the next release. If the PR is still red at a head the driver produced and main has not moved, go to the hand-back.
- **Case 2, or case 1 still red:** hand the failure back to the batch session, the way #959 does. Send it the PR, the failing sha, the failing check names and an instruction to fix and push, leaving the draft/ready state alone. Do it once per (PR, sha) and only when the session is idle, the same rule that already holds conflict hand-backs while a session is working ("nothing sent, retried next pass").
- A red PR the driver has handed back appears under **Needs you now** only once the hand-back fails or the session is gone. Until then it is in progress, not blocked.

## Relation to #1062

#1062 (merge queue on main) removes most case-1 reds at the source: nothing lands on main without being tested against current main, so a broken main snapshot like this one should not exist. It does not remove the need for recovery. A repo without a required merge queue, a red caused by the batch's own work, or a flaky main still leaves a stepped-over PR with no owner. This issue is that recovery path; under #1062 it would apply to a PR dropped from the queue.

## Acceptance

- A batch PR made red by a driver update, with main later fixed, is updated again and merges without operator or manual action.
- A batch PR red at a session commit is handed back exactly once per sha, and the session's push turns it green and lets it re-enter the train.
- Repeated passes over the same red sha send nothing new.
